column1: # OCR-BAKEOFF (lighton-print, 2026-10-15): LightOnOCR-3-4B on the bake-off sample, scored beside Falcon-OCR.
# Build: prithivMLmods/LightOnOCR-3-4B-MLX 8bit/ (revision e93084a, hw-panel's), linked as $OCRLAB/mlx/LightOnOCR-3-4B-8bit
# and read by bakeoff.sh --build lighton3 (bakeoff-models.tsv row lightonocr-3-4b-8bit): empty prompt, --max-side 2048
# --max-tokens 4096 (the card's), whole pages and crops exactly as the others, under run-guarded.sh (12 GB kill). The job
# held the machine-wide heavy lock for its whole run (20:03-22:04), so the times are a quiet machine's.
# Scored by ops/ocrlab/score-bakeoff.py over every saved reading; the columns are OCR-BAKEOFF-2026-10-07.tsv's (its header
# says what each means). falcon-ocr-bf16's and vision's rows are the same run of the scorer and reproduce that file's
# figures exactly, so the scorer and the sample are unchanged. Falcon's times are its 2026-10-07 job's.
# RESULT: LightOnOCR-3-4B misses more words than Falcon-OCR on every class (old print 0.61% vs 0.23%, newspapers 0.86%
# vs 0.52%, modern 1.20% vs 0.63%), and is three times slower (39 s a page whole vs 12, 103 s as crops vs 30). It fits:
# no page killed or cut, peak 7.9 GB (Falcon 4.5), over ModelGuard's default 5 GB cap. Its losses are spread, mostly
# skipped lines: s46 and s43 (newspapers, 62 and 36 more words missed than Falcon), s20 (modern, 9.6%), s09 (old,
# 10.9%: it drops the figure's caption and the three lines under the figure). Not queued for print.
